clue.text: Pestered, say, by an ill-tempered old woman

indicators.note: say tells the solver to go by how the word for pestered is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: pestered means harried, harassed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being nagged by a cantankerous old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a sound-alike: HARRIED spoken quickly runs into HARRID, and 'by' simply joins it to AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew or scold: the word names a bad-tempered, bossy older woman.

clue.text: Bill and Cyril manufactured synthetic fibre

parts.note: AC, account, is a bill

indicators.note: manufactured means made up, so the name's letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: Bill and Cyril produced an artificial textile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name beside Cyril; it is AC (account). 'manufactured' turns CYRIL into RYLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-made polymer spun into yarn for clothing.

clue.text: Proper worker and one's chief assistant, this man

parts.note: proper means right, correct
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A proper workman is the boss's main helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this man' tells you to add 'man' to the answer to get the phrase for a chief assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's most trusted aide is their right-hand man.

clue.text: Hold and let baby sit on one's knee apparently

indicators.note: apparently means plainly to be seen, so the letters are in view within the words

explanation.surface: Hold a baby and let it sit on your knee.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in holD AND LEt; 'apparently' signals it is there in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To bounce a small child on one's lap.

clue.text: Prison register as a novel means of entering the roll of saints

parts.note: novel means new
a gate is a way in
the church calendar lists saints' days

explanation.surface: A record of convicts is described as a fresh route into sainthood.
explanation.walkthrough: The Newgate Calendar was a popular record of crimes and executions linked to Newgate, London's notorious old prison. 'novel' suggests a book but means new.
explanation.definitionFit: A published record of the inmates and executions of a famous London jail.

clue.text: Indian sort of dance

explanation.surface: A dance is said to come from an Indian people.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a Native American people of the Southwest, and a violent Parisian street dance named after them.

clue.text: Songsmith's skill shown in a flying machine

parts.note: a songsmith's product is an air, a tune
craft means skill

explanation.surface: A songwriter's talent is on display in an aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: A songsmith's skill is AIR CRAFT, the craft of writing airs.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeroplane, helicopter or similar vehicle for travel through the sky.

clue.text: Worry about container for firearm

indicators.note: the word for worry goes round the container

parts.note: care means worry
a bin is a container

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a case for a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worry about' reads as fretting over something, but 'about' is the container signal wrapping the container word.
explanation.definitionFit: A short rifle originally carried by cavalry.

clue.text: Cosmetic woad? Yes, he could make it

indicators.note: the letters could be made into the product by reordering them

explanation.surface: Woad, the ancient blue dye, could be turned into make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make it' rearranges WOADYESHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-up applied to the eyelids, a beauty product.

clue.text: Transvestite may be seen with this monster

definitions.text: Transvestite may be seen with this

explanation.surface: A cross-dresser appears alongside a fearsome beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as DRAG ON: a transvestite may be seen with drag on, that is, wearing the clothes of the other sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-dresser wears drag clothing; the other sense is the fire-breathing creature of legend.

clue.text: Veteran fighter's inferior with-out a right hand

indicators.note: split as 'with out', the word for inferior has the other pieces placed within it, its letters on the outside

parts.note: inferior means worse
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old soldier is thought lesser for lacking a right hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'with-out' disguises the container: A, R and H go inside WORSE; 'fighter's' is read as 'fighter is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old campaigner, originally a horse ridden in battle, now any seasoned fighter.

clue.text: Naval unit 'heading from Liverpool, all of it destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed says the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in another order
the heading of a word is its first letter, so only the start of Liverpool is used

explanation.surface: A naval squadron leaving Liverpool is wiped out to the last ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' shuffles L (the heading from Liverpool) with ALLOFIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fleet of ships or boats, a group within a navy.

clue.text: Vegetable on the gunners' menu

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, is the British army's gunners
a menu lists dishes, so an item on it is a dish

explanation.surface: A vegetable appears on the soldiers' bill of fare.
explanation.walkthrough: The gunners' dish is RA DISH: RA is the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp red root eaten raw in salads, a garden vegetable.

clue.text: A little bit of a fight

explanation.surface: There was only a small amount of fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment or morsel, and also a scuffle or brawl.

clue.text: Crossing the — Thames at Bab-lock-hithe" (Arnold)

parts.note: a missing word from Matthew Arnold's poem The Scholar-Gipsy, describing the young river near its source

explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in Matthew Arnold's line from The Scholar-Gipsy; Bablock Hythe is a crossing of the upper Thames in Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth: the upper Thames is pictured as a slender young river.

clue.text: Mrs Swan, a Quaker, maybe a woman of letters

parts.note: a female swan is called a pen
Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends

explanation.surface: A Quaker lady named Swan may be a literary figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woman of letters' suggests an author, but here it is someone who writes letters to a distant correspondent.
explanation.definitionFit: A correspondent one knows only through exchanging post, who may well be female.

clue.text: The Italian record I state is contrary to reason

parts.note: il is Italian for the
a log is a record
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: An Italian's records are called unreasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Italian' is IL, the Italian word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Not following sound reasoning; senseless.

clue.text: Swinger has fruit without end, you say?

annotationWithheld.why: Swinger has fruit without end, you say? (8) for PENDULUM: LUM (plum without its end) and U (you, say) are visible, but no clue word gives PEND
annotationWithheld.clue: Swinger has fruit without end, you say?

clue.text: With which one makes way

parts.note: read literally, the material a road builder uses to make a way, a road surface

explanation.definitionFit: Broken stone laid as the foundation of a road, what a highway is built from.

clue.text: Arabian bird found in this 6 ac state

definitions.text: Arabian bird found in this 6 ac state

parts.words: Arabian bird found in this 6 ac state
parts.note: the Arabian bird is the phoenix of legend, and a city with that name is the capital of a state where the Indians of 6 across lived

explanation.walkthrough: Phoenix, the mythical Arabian bird, is also the state capital, and the Apache people of 6 across lived there.
explanation.definitionFit: A southwestern US state, home to Apache peoples and with Phoenix as its capital.

clue.text: Bender that's lifted during one

parts.note: a bender is a drinking spree, and the arm's bending joint is raised with each drink

explanation.surface: Something is raised during a drinking binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bender' first suggests a binge, and 'one' refers back to it; the joint that bends the arm is the thing lifted, as in 'lifting the elbow' for drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint in the arm, which bends, and which a drinker raises glass after glass.

clue.text: To Lorna — uncommonly tasty bird

indicators.note: uncommonly means unusually, so the name's letters are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: Lorna is told the dish is unusually delicious poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncommonly' rearranges TOLORNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bunting eaten as a French delicacy.

clue.text: Some 50% were wont to be drunk

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word some is taken, its front half

parts.note: were wont to means used to

explanation.surface: Half of them used to be heavy drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: '50%' gives SO, the first half of 'Some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaked in drink, intoxicated.

clue.text: Prepared to fire the first leader of dissidents

parts.note: prime means first in rank or order

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only the start of dissidents is used

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to shoot the chief of the rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fire the first' reads as sacking the chief, but 'Prepared to fire' is the definition: a gun is primed.
explanation.definitionFit: A primed gun has its charge ready, so it is all set for shooting.

clue.text: A note — leg broken — what can a stretcher do?

indicators.note: a broken leg is a common sight on a stretcher, but here broken asks for the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A message reports a broken leg; what can the ambulance stretcher do?
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' shuffles ANOTE and LEG; 'stretcher' suggests a medical litter but means anything that stretches.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stretches makes things longer, which is what lengthen means.

clue.text: Club, mid-second century, used in the main battle

parts.note: an iron is a kind of golf club
the middle of the second century is the year 150, written CL in Roman numerals, followed by AD

explanation.surface: A club from around the year 150 was wielded in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the sea, so the battle is a naval one.
explanation.definitionFit: A nineteenth-century warship armoured with metal plates, fought at sea.

clue.text: Thus large deer retreating from the peasant's blade

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word for the deer is read in reverse

parts.note: an elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: A big deer backs away from a farm worker's cutting tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns the deer backwards (KLE); 'from' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved, hand-held harvesting tool, the emblem of the peasantry.

clue.text: The Boy King is a ranting actor

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's royal cipher
taken as written
a ham is an actor who overplays

explanation.surface: The young monarch is an over-the-top performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Boy King' suggests Tutankhamun, but 'Boy' is the definition and 'is' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so an example of a boy's name.

clue.text: Suggestive of hand-out landlord's due to receive

indicators.note: the landlord's payment takes in the other piece, receiving it inside

parts.note: rent is what a tenant owes the landlord
dole is a hand-out, especially state benefit

explanation.surface: A hand-out hints at the money owed to a landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to receive' is the container signal; 'of' belongs with the definition, as in 'redolent of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Evocative or reminiscent, as a scent recalls a place.
